title: A mel spectrogram without an FFT

children.author: rkoch
children.text:
Did you compare against a Goertzel bank? For a handful of bins it is usually the cheapest thing on a small FPGA.

Curious what the LE count looks like.

children.author: oskar
children.text: Briefly. Goertzel gives one bin per instance, and the upper mel bands are wide, so I would need several per band. One biquad covers a band.

children.author: rkoch
children.text: Fair, the bandwidth is the catch.

children.author: lowpass_
children.text: How sensitive is the classifier to the exact filter shapes? I would expect the first conv layer to absorb a fair amount of mismatch. See this paper.

children.author: mjd
children.text:
Same experience here. The first layer quietly fixes whatever the front end gets slightly wrong.

  y[n] = b0*x[n] + b1*x[n-1]

children.author: tinyml_fan
children.text: Would like to see LE and multiplier usage once the inference engine is in.
